nodes.description: DVL proteins route canonical and noncanonical WNT signals. DVL3 terminal variants are proposed to perturb phosphorylation, localization, multimerization or receptor interactions, but their physiological signaling effect has not been established by the cited patient studies. Context-dependent DVL1 reporter and localization results do not determine the DVL3 mechanism.

evidence.reference_title: Novel pathogenic variants and quantitative phenotypic analyses of Robinow syndrome: WNT signaling perturbation and phenotypic variability.
evidence.snippet: Robinow syndrome (RS) is a genetically heterogeneous disorder with six genes that converge on the WNT/planar cell polarity (PCP) signaling pathway implicated (DVL1, DVL3, FZD2, NXN, ROR2, and WNT5A).

nodes.description: The altered frame replaces the native DVL3 C terminus with a distinctive peptide, while preserving upstream functional domains. The 2018 sequence analysis identifies 83 shared novel residues before the stop codon. Sequence inference and RNA detection do not establish mutant protein stability, localization or signaling direction in patient tissues.

evidence.reference_title: Autosomal dominant Robinow syndrome associated with a novel DVL3 splice mutation.
evidence.snippet: mutant DVL3 proteins associated with Robinow syndrome show truncation of the C-terminus and share 83 novel amino acid residues before the stop codon

nodes.description: Selected coding and splice variants generate the characteristic minus-one frame. In the 2018 c.1715-2A>C case, patient RNA showed deletion of four nucleotides at the start of exon 15. The two 2016 splice substitutions were instead predicted to use a cryptic acceptor two bases downstream; that computational result must not be confused with the later observed four-base deletion.

evidence.reference_title: Autosomal dominant Robinow syndrome associated with a novel DVL3 splice mutation.
evidence.snippet: Mutant DVL3 mRNAs were found to harbor a deletion of four nucleotides at the beginning of exon 15 and encode a protein product with a distinct -1 reading-frame C-terminus.

nodes.description: DVL3 disease affects limb development, causing variable shortening and digital anomalies. The reported patient series do not directly measure growth-plate polarity or chondrocyte differentiation; Ror2-null and DVL1 overexpression findings cannot establish a DVL3-specific cellular lesion. Pectus excavatum is also reported in a molecularly characterized DVL3 patient. Radial head dislocation, hemivertebrae and scoliosis are retained from the cross-genotype GeneReviews baseline; unlike the primary DVL3 digit and pectus findings cited here, these sources do not establish a DVL3-specific developmental association, so this node does not assign them a causal edge.
